basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 3.' and it opens '(Cap. XLIX.—Vers. 3.) Ruben primogenitus meus, tu fortitudo mea et principium filiorum'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLIX.—Vers. 3.) Ruben primogenitus meus, tu fortitudo mea et principium filiorum meorum, durus ad ferendum et durus procacitate, et injuria, sicut aqua non ebullias. Ascendisti enim super lectulum patris tui. Tunc violasti stratum, cum ascendisti. In Hebraeo scriptum est: Ruben primogenitus meus, tu fortitudo mea, et capitulum in liberis meis. Major ad portandum, et major robore. Effusus es sicut aqua, ne adjicias. Ascendisti enim cubile patris tui, et contaminasti stratum in ascensu. Est autem sensus hic: Tu es primogenitus meus, major in liberis, et debebas juxta ordinem nativitatis tuae, haereditatem, quae primogenitis jure debebatur, et sacerdotium accipere et regnum: hoc quippe in portando onere et praevalido robore demonstratur. Verum quia peccasti, et quasi aqua, quae vasculo non tenetur, voluptatis impetu effusus es, idcirco praecipio tibi, ut ultra non pecces, sisque in fratrum numero, poenam peccati luens, quod primogeniti ordinem perdidisti.
